title: We Don't Exist Announces: Play as Bigfoot and Mothman Instead of Hunting Them

content:
Solo developer Versiris has announced We Don't Exist, a story-driven adventure game that flips the cryptid genre's standard premise on its head: instead of hunting Bigfoot, you eventually become him. Revealed today with an announcement trailer, first screenshots, and a live Steam wishlist page, the game lets players step into the roles of Bigfoot, Mothman, and the Jersey Devil as fully realized characters — each with their own voice-acted narrative arc woven into an interdimensional conspiracy that threatens both the human world and the hidden cryptid realm alongside it. No release date has been set.

When You Find Bigfoot, You Fall Into His World

The premise of We Don't Exist begins somewhere familiar — a Bigfoot hunter out alone at night — and then does something genuinely unexpected with it. While searching for the elusive creature one night, the player character stumbles upon a parallel dimension sitting alongside our own, one where Bigfoot, Mothman, the Jersey Devil, and other creatures of American folklore are not only real but have lives, personalities, and stakes in what happens next. A shadowy interdimensional conspiracy threatens both worlds, and it falls to the player and their new cryptid companions to uncover the truth before it's too late.

What makes that premise notable is who gets to narrate it. We Don't Exist doesn't just cast the cryptids as companions — it makes them playable protagonists. Players will be able to switch into the role of Mothman, the Jersey Devil, and other famous creatures, experiencing the conspiracy from inside each creature's own perspective, with distinct character arcs that feed into the larger story. That's a structural choice that transforms what could have been a paranormal tourism game into something closer to an ensemble drama staged in folklore. The game's Steam page is now live and open for wishlisting.

What Makes This a Solo Achievement Worth Watching

The most striking thing about We Don't Exist is not its premise, impressive as that is — it's who's building it. Versiris is the solo developer moniker of Tanya Kozak, a Philadelphia-based artist, animator, programmer, and designer who previously served on the art team for Drinkbox Studios' Guacamelee (2013) and Guacamelee 2 (2018). The production scope she has committed to for her debut rivals what small teams typically attempt: full voice acting across a cast of hand-drawn characters, multiple playable protagonists each with their own story arcs, a dynamic dialogue system in which characters remember the player's choices and expressed preferences, free-roam areas with optional side-stories, and a collectibles log tracking the creatures and curios encountered across the game.

That scope has been made achievable by the choice of engine. The official press kit for We Don't Exist confirms the game is built in Unreal Engine 5, which Epic Games made free to use under a revenue-share model. UE5's Lumen lighting and Nanite geometry systems enable a single developer to achieve cinematic-quality environments without a dedicated art team — a meaningful shift from conditions that made comparable solo ambition impractical even a few years ago. The Steam page's minimum system requirements — a quad-core processor, 32 GB of RAM, and a DirectX 12 graphics card with 8 GB of VRAM — reflect the engine's footprint.

That context matters for anyone assessing Versiris's ambition. Stardew Valley's Eric Barone, Undertale's Toby Fox, Axiom Verge's Thomas Happ, and Braid's Jonathan Blow each produced breakthrough solo games — but those were games built in accessible 2D engines or small-team workflows. A voiced, multi-protagonist adventure with a fully realized 2.5D parallel world is a step up in production ambition. Whether the execution matches the scope is a question only the finished game can answer, but the announced feature set signals a developer with a specific and well-considered vision for what they want to make.

Dialogue That Listens and Remembers

One of We Don't Exist's most technically ambitious promises is its dynamic conversation system. According to the developer, the NPCs and cryptid companions won't just offer static dialogue trees — they'll remember what the player says across conversations, tracking their stated preferences, past choices, and even the things they've revealed about themselves. That kind of persistent memory system, sometimes called "relationship tracking" or "dynamic NPC memory," has appeared in games ranging from the early interactive drama Façade to Baldur's Gate 3's companion reactivity, but implementing it as a solo developer across a full cast of voiced, hand-drawn characters is a meaningful design and engineering challenge. The dynamic conversations feature is listed as a core pillar of the game's design on the Steam page.

Why Bigfoot, Mothman, and the Jersey Devil?

The three creatures at the center of We Don't Exist aren't arbitrary picks. Bigfoot, also known as Sasquatch, is arguably the most-discussed cryptid in America, with reported sightings going back to the 19th century, active enthusiast organizations, and a dedicated museum in Boring, Oregon. Mothman emerged from Point Pleasant, West Virginia in 1966 and became embedded in American popular consciousness through John Keel's 1975 book The Mothman Prophecies and the 2002 film — Point Pleasant now hosts an annual Mothman Festival drawing tens of thousands of visitors each year. The Jersey Devil has haunted the Pine Barrens of southern New Jersey in folklore for more than 250 years, with sightings so persistent that a $250,000 reward was reportedly offered for its capture in 1960.

These creatures share a defining quality: they're not generic monsters. Each has a specific geography, a specific cultural moment that made them famous, and a community of people who care about them. Casting them as protagonists with their own story arcs in We Don't Exist gives Versiris pre-built emotional investment to work with.

Is We Don't Exist a Horror Game?

We Don't Exist carries a distinctive tone — eerie, conspiratorial, with undertones of genuine mystery about what the interdimensional threat actually is — but it's not a horror game in the conventional sense. The hand-drawn art style leans into atmosphere rather than gore, and the emphasis on forming relationships with the cryptid companions and completing rewarding side-stories signals that warmth and character connection are as central to the design as the mystery. The Steam community tags include Adventure, Narrative, Atmospheric, Supernatural, and Mystery — alongside Werewolves, Aliens, and Conspiracy — which collectively sketch a game interested in the strange and uncanny without defaulting to jump-scare mechanics. Think closer to a paranormal drama with exploration and collectibles than a creature-feature survival game.

What You Can Do Now

We Don't Exist does not have a release date, but the Steam page is live at store.steampowered.com/app/4489610/We_Dont_Exist/ and open for wishlisting. Versiris maintains a YouTube channel at youtube.com/@Versiris where the announcement trailer is available, an official site at wedontexist.fyi, and an X account at x.com/Versiris for development updates. At launch, the game will support English with full audio and subtitles.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is We Don't Exist?

We Don't Exist is a story-driven adventure game announced in October 2026 by solo developer Versiris. Players explore a parallel dimension where creatures like Bigfoot, Mothman, and the Jersey Devil are real, and help their cryptid companions unravel an interdimensional conspiracy threatening both worlds. The game features full voice acting, a hand-drawn art style, character customization, and a dynamic dialogue system where NPCs remember the player's choices and preferences. It is planned for PC via Steam with no release date yet announced. More details are available on the official Steam wishlist page.

Can you actually play as Bigfoot or Mothman?

Yes. We Don't Exist goes beyond the typical setup of a player character who talks to monsters — it lets players take control of famous cryptids including Mothman and the Jersey Devil as playable protagonists. Each cryptid has their own character arc within the game's larger narrative, and their interconnected stories are part of how the conspiracy unfolds. The feature is listed as a core mechanic on the Steam page under "Take On Multiple Roles."

How ambitious is it for a solo developer to build this game?

Very. We Don't Exist targets a production scope that has historically required small teams: full voice acting, multiple playable characters each with their own narrative arcs, a dialogue memory system, free-roam areas, and a hand-drawn visual style. The game is confirmed to be built on Unreal Engine 5 — a free-to-use engine that has meaningfully changed what a single developer can produce in terms of visual quality and cinematic scope. Successful solo games like Stardew Valley and Undertale set a high bar; We Don't Exist is aiming for a more cinematically complex form of that ambition.

Where can you wishlist We Don't Exist?

The game's Steam page is live now at store.steampowered.com/app/4489610/We_Dont_Exist/. You can also follow development at the official site wedontexist.fyi or on X at x.com/Versiris. No release date has been announced.
